q: Does a milk run cut emissions compared with direct deliveries from each supplier?
title: Milk run vs direct delivery emissions
short: Compare the fuel of one truck collecting from several suppliers on a loop against separate trucks from each supplier. Multiply litres by 2.68 kg CO2 per litre for each case. A milk run usually cuts distance and empty running, provided the truck is full enough.

ul: Total distance for the loop against the sum of direct trips.
Litres per km for each truck size, from fuel records.
Load factor, since a half-empty loop truck saves less.

p: Inbound freight you pay for is Scope 3, Category 4. Your own trucks running the loop are Scope 1.
Keep the planned and actual routes and fuel. A before and after figure from real fuel use is stronger than a modelled one.

example.title: Worked example: five suppliers (one trip, illustrative inputs)
lines: Direct: five suppliers, five trucks, 120 km each at an assumed 5 km per litre: 600 / 5 = 120 litres x 2.68 = 321.6 kg CO2
Milk run: one truck, 140 km loop at an assumed 4.5 km per litre: 31.11 litres x 2.68 = 83.38 kg CO2
example.note: Distances and mileages are assumed inputs.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and fuel card statements (diesel 2.68 and CNG 2.69 kg CO2, IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 record. Hired transport goes to the Scope 3 evidence trail, and distance or tonne-km estimates are labelled as estimates.
